t: Married as a child to the raja of Jhansi, Lakshmibai lost her infant son and then her husband, and the East India Company annexed Jhansi in 1854 under the doctrine of lapse in spite of her appeals.
After sepoys mutinied at Jhansi in June 1857 and nearly all the British there were killed, she took over its rule; whether she took part in the killings was and remains contested.
Hugh Rose captured Jhansi in April 1858, and she died fighting at Gwalior that June; she became a heroine of Indian nationalism, a reading that Dalit writers dispute.
dyk: In 1943 Subhas Chandra Bose, recognising the Rani's symbolism, called for female volunteers for the Indian National Army, who were formed into the Rani of Jhansi Regiment and trained in Singapore.
ev: Manikarnika Tambe is born in Varanasi, a date placed between 1828 and 1830 by Roy and Mukherjee but given as 1827 or 1835 in other sources
According to Indian sources, she marries the raja of Jhansi, Gangadhar Rao, in May and becomes the Rani Lakshmibai
She gives birth to a son, who dies at a few months old
Gangadhar Rao adopts Damodar Rao and dies on 21 November
The Company rejects her appeals, and Jhansi lapses to it in May
Sepoys mutiny at Jhansi in June, most of the British are killed on 8 June, and she proclaims her rule on the sepoys' departure
Hugh Rose besieges Jhansi from 22 March; the town falls on 3 April and she escapes from the fort that night
She dies in battle near Gwalior on 18 June, and Rose captures the city the next day

f.born: Varanasi, as Manikarnika Tambe, called Manu; daughter of Moropant Tambe, a Karhada Brahmin in the service of the Maratha noble Chimaji, and Bhagirathi. Her birth year is disputed: 1827 in British sources, 1835 in most Indian sources, between 1828 and 1830 for the historians Tapti Roy and Rudrangshu Mukherjee
f.died: 18 June 1858, in battle against British forces near Gwalior; the exact manner of her death is unknown, but all accounts agree she died fighting
f.role: Queen consort of the princely state of Jhansi from 1843 to 1853; leader of Jhansi from June 1857 until the British captured it in April 1858; one of the leading figures of the Indian Rebellion of 1857
f.known: her appeals against the annexation of Jhansi under the doctrine of lapse; her rule of Jhansi in 1857 to 1858; the Siege of Jhansi and her escape from the fort; the last stand at Gwalior; the contested question of her part in the killing of the British at Jhansi; her place in Indian nationalism
